verses.text: Then some Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem and asked,
“Why do your disciples break the elders’ tradition? They don’t wash their hands before they eat.”
He answered, “Why do you break God’s command because of your tradition?
God said, ‘Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘Whoever speaks evil of their father or mother must be put to death.’
But you say, ‘If anyone tells their father or mother, “Whatever help you could have received from me is a gift dedicated to God,”
they don’t have to honor their father or mother.’ So you’ve canceled God’s command to keep your tradition.
You hypocrites! Isaiah was right when he prophesied about you:
‘These people honor me with their words, but their hearts are far from me.
Their worship means nothing, because they teach human rules as if they were God’s commands.’”
Jesus called the crowd over and said, “Listen and understand this:
What goes into a person’s mouth doesn’t make them unclean. What comes out of the mouth is what makes them unclean.”
Then the disciples came to him and said, “Do you know the Pharisees were offended when they heard that?”
He answered, “Every plant my Father in heaven didn’t plant will be pulled up.
Leave them alone. They’re blind guides. If a blind person guides another blind person, they’ll both fall into a pit.”
Peter said to him, “Explain this parable to us.”
Jesus said, “You still don’t understand?
Don’t you see that whatever enters the mouth passes into the stomach and then out of the body?
But what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart, and that is what makes a person unclean.
Evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and insults against God all come from the heart.
Those are the things that make a person unclean. Eating with unwashed hands doesn’t.”
Jesus left there and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
A Canaanite woman from that region came out and shouted, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is suffering terribly because of a demon!”
Jesus didn’t answer her. His disciples came and urged him, “Send her away, because she keeps shouting after us.”
He answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel.”
But she came and bowed before him, saying, “Lord, help me.”
He replied, “It isn’t right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
She said, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their owners’ table.”
Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, your faith is great! Let it happen just as you want.” Her daughter was healed at that moment.
Jesus left there and went along the Sea of Galilee. He went up a mountain and sat down.
Large crowds came to him, bringing people who were lame, blind, unable to speak, disabled, and many others. They laid them at his feet, and he healed them.
The crowd was amazed to see those who couldn’t speak talking, the disabled healed, the lame walking, and the blind seeing. They praised the God of Israel.

Jesus called his disciples and said, “I feel compassion for this crowd. They’ve stayed with me for three days and have nothing to eat. I don’t want to send them away hungry in case they collapse on the way.”
The disciples said, “Where could we get enough bread in this deserted place to feed such a huge crowd?”
Jesus asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They answered, “Seven, and a few small fish.”
He told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
He took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them, and handed them to his disciples, who distributed them to the crowd.
Everyone ate and was satisfied. The disciples collected seven baskets full of leftover pieces.
Four thousand men ate, not counting the women and children.
After sending the crowds away, Jesus got into a boat and went to the region of Magdala.
